activity.notes: Tōgō Heihachirō (1847–1934) commanded the Imperial Japanese Navy's Combined Fleet during the 1905 Battle of Tsushima against the Russian Baltic Fleet in the Russo-Japanese War. This records his directly sourced naval command and battle, not a claim that he alone determined the war's outcome. 1905 is a one-year representative military activity, not his full 1903–1905 tenure. The 1868–1945 Empire of Japan is the canonical historical polity; no new Japanese state, territory or fleet-polity identity is created.

sources.title: Togo Heihachiro — Japan Center for Asian Historical Records, National Archives of Japan
sources.citation_text: Japan's archival exhibition identifies Togo as 1903 Combined Fleet commander and lists the Russo-Japanese War and Battle of Tsushima among the fleet engagements under his command.

sources.title: Part 2 Chapter 5: Military men in Russo-Japanese War — National Diet Library Japan
sources.citation_text: Japan's National Diet Library records Togo as commander-in-chief of the Combined Fleet that defeated the Russian Baltic Fleet at Tsushima.

sources.title: Admiral of the Fleet Count Heihachiro Togo — Royal Museums Greenwich
sources.citation_text: The UK national maritime museum corroborates Togo's personal identity, dates, and command of Japan's victorious fleet at Tsushima, 1905.
